rows.statement: Before spawn the host plans the exact host-to-worker frame sequence and measures every frame as its deterministic-CBOR envelope payload; the 40-byte prefix is excluded from every limit (rust2 lengthScope 'payload bytes only' and aggregateAccounting). A planned frame over maxFramePayloadBytes (both majors; includes the one-frame SnapshotManifest, DependencySourceManifest and PreparedOutputManifest) or, for major 3, a request over maxRequestPayloadBytesTotal or maxRequestFrames refuses as native.provider-request-exceeds-wire-limit. Chunks are greedy: each chunk carries the maximum chunk bytes except the last; zero-length entries have no chunk. One maximal Cancel is reserved. maxRequestFrames is not reachable by inputs the other admissions accept (check computes the bound) but is still enforced.
rows.justification: Owner limits make over-frame manifests (>~578k minimal dependency entries; 256 prepared rows with 1024x256 configurations) and over-total requests (8 GiB snapshot + 8 GiB dependency + 1 GiB prepared > 9 GiB) reachable; a host that cannot send them would otherwise misclassify reachable input as a protocol or host fault.
